paper_title: DTaPO: Dynamic Thermal-Aware Performance Optimization for Dark Silicon Many-Core Systems

extraction.paper_title: DTaPO: Dynamic Thermal-Aware Performance Optimization for Dark Silicon Many-Core Systems

scenario.figure_or_table: Section 4.1 and Table 4; Figure 10 (slowdown and Tmax/Tavg/Tmin across DTM techniques and thresholds); Figure 4 (floorplan)
scenario.description: DTaPO (task migration plus DVFS) evaluated on a simulated 64-core NoC many-core system, with 32 active and 32 dark cores in a chessboard pattern. The workload mixes radix, ocean, blackscholes and bodytrack with 8 threads each. Thresholds range from 60 to 85 C, compared against DVFS-only and no-DTM baselines. Core size is 2.95 mm x 2.95 mm. No per-core power values or absolute core coordinates are published in the paper text.
scenario.architecture: 64-core homogeneous 22 nm NoC many-core (8x8 mesh, 4 GHz max, 32 KB L1-I/L1-D, 512 KB L2 per core, 8 MB L3 per 8 cores), 2D planar die, HotSpot ceramic BGA package stack with heat spreader and heat sink
scenario.workload: Mix of Splash-2 radix and ocean and PARSEC blackscholes and bodytrack, 8 threads each, run on 32 active cores
scenario.operating_point: Threshold temperatures 60-85 C (epsilon 5 C, frequency step 200 MHz, Fthr 3.6 GHz), ambient 318.15 K, 50% dark silicon

original_setup.solver: LifeSim toolchain: Sniper performance simulation, McPAT power estimation (22 nm), and HotSpot (HotSpot 6.0 cited) transient thermal simulation with a stacked ceramic BGA package model (Section 4.1, PDF pp. 8-10, Table 4 on p. 11)
original_setup.optimizer: No formal numerical optimizer. DTaPO is a heuristic runtime algorithm (Algorithm 1, p. 8) that minimizes makespan subject to Ti < Tthr for all cores (Eq. 3, p. 7). Parameters epsilon = 5 C, frequency step = 200 MHz and Fthr = 3.6 GHz were set empirically (p. 10).
original_setup.controller: DTaPO: periodic threshold-based dynamic thermal management. It sees transient core temperatures, migrates tasks one way from hot active cores to cooler dark cores within an LLC-sharing cluster, and falls back to stepwise DVFS when no cooler core is available. The 64 cores sit in an 8x8 mesh with a 50% chessboard active/dark pattern (pp. 5-8).
original_setup.benchmark: 64-core 22 nm NoC many-core system with 32 active and 32 dark cores. Workload mix: Splash-2 radix and ocean plus PARSEC blackscholes and bodytrack, 8 threads each (Table 3, p. 10). Thresholds 60-85 C are compared against DVFS-only and no-DTM baselines (Figure 10, p. 13). A separate 10-application comparison against OSP uses TDP = 42 W (Figure 12, p. 15).

thermal_observable.unit: degC (reduction in average peak temperature of DTaPO relative to DVFS-only; a delta, not an absolute temperature)
thermal_observable.location: Per-core transient temperatures of the simulated 64-core chip, with peak taken over the cores. The paper states the maximum and minimum are represented by the 90th and 10th percentiles of the fluctuating transient temperatures.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Average of 10 repeated runs over the four-application mix, with the reduction reported as the maximum across thresholds (60-85 C). Text on p. 15 and abstract p. 1; per-threshold Tmax/Tavg/Tmin bars are shown in Figure 10 (p. 13) and have not been digitized. A separate 13.6 degC peak reduction vs OSP is reported for the 10-application comparison.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper's result depends on dynamic transient control: closed-loop DTaPO task migration and DVFS, with a 100 us wake-up latency, 1000-cycle migration penalty and cache cold-start effects. A steady-state 2D Studio solve with a fixed placement and a one-row power trace cannot reproduce the controller behavior or the dynamic thermal results.

The paper publishes no per-core or per-block power values, only that McPAT was used. Per-core power cannot be split from a total, since no total chip power or splitting rule is given. Core absolute coordinates are also not published; only the core size (2.95 mm x 2.95 mm) and the chessboard pattern are given.

The paper's solver is the coupled Sniper/McPAT/HotSpot/LifeSim toolchain with a CBGA package: heat spreader, heat sink with R = 0.1 K/W, TIM, ceramic substrate and printed board. A Studio solver with different package/cooling assumptions would not match it. The 3D, interposer and chiplet aspects are not applicable, because the paper uses a monolithic 2D planar die.

The optimizer and workload are architecture-level: DVFS levels, task mapping and multi-threaded benchmarks over time-varying power. No optimizer is involved in the Studio setup and no placement optimization is performed. The paper also covers no reliability analysis and no 3D stacking.

methods.note: The paper text supports the Sniper/McPAT/HotSpot (LifeSim) toolchain and the Algorithm 1 task-migration plus DVFS controller (pp. 7-10). The extraction's experiment.kind 'custom_2d_steady' contradicts the paper's closed-loop transient method and its own steady_2d_relevant=false. The 'CBGA package model' wording is also overstated, because Figure 6 is only a 'typical' CBGA stack adapted from [37]. Nothing in the paper confirms the simulated package used exactly those layers.

code.note: The packet has no assets, and the paper has no code, repository, or data-availability statement (pp. 16-18). No LifeSim/Sniper/McPAT/HotSpot modification code or config files were supplied, so none can be verified.

parameters.note: Text-verified against the PDF: 2.95 mm core (p.8, Fig 4 p.9), 64 cores, 4 GHz, 32 active cores (p.10), eps 5 C, step 200 MHz, Fthr 3.6 GHz (p.10), threshold range 60-85 C (p.11), Table 4 values (p.11), 100 us wake-up (p.9), 1000-cycle penalty (p.12), and TDP 42 W for the OSP comparison only (p.15). Ambiguities remain: the OSP comparison gives eps = 0.5 without units, and the Table 1 symbol Δf versus ζ in Algorithm 1 is inconsistent. The 10.8 C aggregation is not verified (see findings).

The extraction states the HotSpot model uses a CBGA package stack with a ceramic substrate and printed board. The paper shows this only as 'a typical CBGA package (adapted from Figure 2 in [37])' (Fig 6) and Table 4 gives only silicon, spreader, TIM, and sink parameters. There is no confirmation that the simulated package included the ceramic substrate or printed board, and no layer dimensions are given.

findings.reason: The paper never says 'monolithic 2D planar die'. This is an inference from the lack of any 3D stacking. It is not an explicit statement.
The scenario is cited to pdf_page 10, but Table 4 is on p.11, Figure 10 on p.13, and Figure 4 on p.9. The page locator is imprecise for the scenario as stated.

The extraction notes eps = 0.5 and Δf = 200 without units for the OSP comparison. These are unresolved and conflict with eps = 5 C and 200 MHz in the main scenario, so the controller parameters are scenario-dependent.
The assets array is empty and no paper-linked repository or supplementary material was found. Claims about code or configs cannot be verified.

The paper says migration is one-way (active to dark), but the conclusion says task migration works 'by swapping tasks among active and dark cores' (p.15-16). Table 1 uses Δf and Algorithm 1 uses ζ, and line 20 uses M[ti] versus Q. The controller specification is therefore ambiguous and not safely implementable from the text.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable. The deterministic gate failed (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, simulation_allowed=false), so Studio did not run: simulation status is skipped, no artifacts exist, and comparison_valid=false. The scenario is the DTaPO threshold sweep on a 64-core 22 nm many-core chip with 32 active and 32 dark cores. It was extracted as a custom_2d_steady experiment, but with no floorplan blocks and no power_w, so it fails the 1–128 block and power_w input requirement. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes, powers or source commit are involved. There is no generated placement, no illustrative input.flp and no one-row input.ptrace. Because a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace, it could not represent the paper's closed-loop transient behavior anyway. The paper's observable is a 10.8 degC reduction in average peak temperature of DTaPO versus DVFS-only. It is a delta, taken as the maximum across the 60-85 degC thresholds, from transient HotSpot results averaged over 10 runs. Since no Studio result exists, no numerical comparison is made and exact replication is not claimed. Qualitatively, the paper reports that task migration to dark cores, with DVFS as a fallback, lowers peak temperature relative to DVFS alone. This is a dynamic-control effect that a steady 2D solve with fixed placement and fixed power cannot test.
limitations: Studio did not run. The gate blocked it because the custom experiment has no blocks and no power_w, and the verdict is not_2d_applicable.
comparison_valid is false. No Studio temperatures exist, and the paper's 10.8 degC delta (and the separate 13.6 degC vs OSP) cannot be compared numerically.

Regime mismatch: the paper uses transient closed-loop DTaPO control (task migration, DVFS, 100 us wake-up, 1000-cycle migration penalty), while a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace and no controller.

Power inputs are missing: the McPAT per-core power values and total chip power are not published, and no power split rule exists. The 42 W TDP applies only to the OSP comparison and must not be split among cores.

Placement inputs are missing: absolute core coordinates, total die size and L3 block size and location are not published. Only the 2.95 mm core size and the chessboard pattern are given, and any generated placement would be illustrative only.

Location and aggregation mismatch: the paper's value is a peak over cores, averaged over 10 runs, as a reduction between two control policies and the maximum across thresholds, with Tmax/Tmin taken as 90th/10th percentiles. This is not a steady-state absolute temperature.

Boundary and package mismatch: the paper uses a HotSpot CBGA stack with heat sink R=0.1 K/W and 318.15 K ambient, but the spreader and sink dimensions and Studio's bundled package assumptions were not supplied.

A steady-state 2D Studio solve with a fixed placement and a one-row power trace cannot reproduce the controller behavior or the dynamic thermal results.

A Studio solver with different package/cooling assumptions would not match it. The 3D, interposer and chiplet aspects are not applicable, because the paper uses a monolithic 2D planar die.
